question: Does ablating one development-selected high-influence MLP column improve exact output contracts beyond matched simpler and random controls?

hypotheses.claim: Ablating the development-selected column improves heldout exact-contract success against strongest simpler arm by at least 5 percentage points
The effect exceeds norm-matched random-column ablation and survives half-strength ablation
Repetitive suffix failure may be reduced by the edit
hypotheses.testability: Only evaluable if development baseline has at least 2 repeated-suffix failures; otherwise NOT_TESTABLE on this model/cohort

prior_exposure: MIT source and PR601 mechanism pilot inspected; all tasks authored by coordinator. No pilot forward inference or outcome exposure before freeze. Evaluation prompts are withheld from algorithmic column selection, not from the coordinator.
reuse: Pinned Smol checkpoint, float32 CPU protocol, activation-to-down_proj boundary and source-byte provenance conventions from PR601. Existing activation-fidelity auditor is unmerged and does not provide checkpoint editing or general correctness guarantees; no unreviewed production dependency copied.

intervention.selection: argmax mean(development final-prompt MLP-input activation squared)*column_L2_squared; lowest index ties
intervention.policy: only one down_proj column, <=576 changed values, <=0.20 tensor relative L2; scale 0 or 0.5; no optimizer or labels

prompt_suffix: Follow the exact requested output format. Check that every requested item is present, use only supplied facts, and stop after the required answer.
grading: Exact text or strict JSON equality; separate deterministic replay. No model grades. Categories are operational proxies, not diagnoses of internal causes.
stopping: No retries, model search, post-outcome prompt/threshold changes or overwrites. Fail on checkpoint/runtime/source mismatch, unsafe edit, or missing matched random column. Preserve failure receipt. Never pool aborted attempts.
analysis: 12 authored heldout tasks +6 regression tasks,3 stochastic seeds each,8 conditions=432 scored generations;6 development baseline generations excluded. Task-cluster bootstrap is descriptive for this finite cohort only. All arms and failures reported.
limits: One-shot output contracts, not multistep agent execution
Public authored exact-match tasks, no external heldout claims
Single pretrained135M checkpoint; no frontier generalization
Random control matches column norm within10%, not semantic selectivity
Projection primitive tested offline but pilot uses ablation; no MIT efficacy replication
Token caps and repetition proxies cannot alone diagnose reasoning loops
No population significance, commercial value, increased intelligence or recursive self-improvement claim
